evidence.detail: Class extends R25 NodeSub, exposes render entrypoints and a model-producing method returning rs/a/h; subclasses include Model itself and the shared actor hierarchy.
Classic client hierarchy uses this NodeSub-derived renderable base between linked-list nodes and Model/Entity-style scene objects.

candidates.note: Renderable is the conservative semantic name for the model-producing scene base.

evidence.detail: Class extends Renderable and owns movement queue arrays, facing/position state, animation/sequence state, hit/combat/status fields, world-point conversion and path update methods.
Both exact NPC and Player classes extend this type directly.
Classic client Entity/Actor base carries the same path queue, animation, facing and hit-state responsibilities for NPCs and players.

candidates.note: Actor is chosen over generic Entity because the class is specifically the shared moving/combat character base.

evidence.detail: Large renderable geometry class owns vertex/face arrays, skin groups, colors/textures/priorities/alphas, bounds, transforms, animation application, projection and rasterization.
R28 Item/NPC/Object/SpotAnimation definitions and Player/Npc rendering all construct or return this exact type.
Layout and rendering surface match the classic client Model class.

candidates.note: Model is fixed by the geometry/render pipeline and definition consumers.

evidence.detail: Class extends Actor and stores one rs/d/d NpcDefinition directly.
Its model/name/combat-level/render methods delegate through the bound NpcDefinition and construct Model instances.
R26 HighlightedNpc stores this exact type and NPC-indicator code consumes it.

candidates.note: Npc is fixed by direct NpcDefinition ownership and actor rendering behavior.

evidence.detail: Class extends Actor, decodes appearance from Stream, owns equipment/color arrays, gender/icon/privilege state, username/display strings and player-specific model assembly.
Exact appearance diagnostic includes gender, headIcon, skullIcon, orbIcon, miscIcon and privilege values.
Structure matches the classic Player class appearance/equipment decode and actor inheritance.

candidates.note: Player is fixed by appearance decoding, player identity fields and model construction.
